title: CVE-2024-6197: freeing stack buffer in utf8asn1str
explain: The code supports the reported flaw. A maintainer should review its impact and decide what to do next.
summary: The report claims that curl's utf8asn1str() function contains an invalid free() call on a stack-allocated buffer, leading to potential memory corruption and control-flow hijacking.

claims.text: Calls free() on a stack-allocated buffer (buf) in utf8asn1str() when wc >= 0x00200000
claims.reasoning: The code at lines 378 and 397 in lib/vtls/x509asn1.c (master) shows buf is a stack-allocated array of 4 chars, and free(buf) is called on it when wc >= 0x00200000. The same bug exists in the release curl-8_8_0 at lines 374 and 393.

citations.note: char buf[4]; /* decode buffer */ - stack allocation
free(buf); - called on stack buffer when wc >= 0x00200000

claims.text: Function utf8asn1str() in lib/vtls/x509asn1.c at line 397
claims.reasoning: The function utf8asn1str is defined starting at line 342, and the free(buf) call is at line 397 in the master branch (line 393 in curl-8_8_0 release).

citations.note: static CURLcode utf8asn1str(struct dynbuf *to, int type, const char *from, const char *end)
free(buf); at line 397 in master (line 393 in curl-8_8_0)

claims.text: Triggered during TLS handshake when parsing a malicious certificate with type CURL_ASN1_UTF8_STRING
claims.reasoning: The vulnerable path is in the else branch (non-UTF8 string types). When type is CURL_ASN1_UNIVERSAL_STRING (size=4), the code reads 4 bytes from the certificate data into wc. If wc >= 0x00200000, the bug triggers. This is reachable during TLS certificate parsing with attacker-controlled certificate data.

citations.note: else branch (type != CURL_ASN1_UTF8_STRING) contains the vulnerable code
switch(size) builds wc from input bytes; for size=4 (CURL_ASN1_UNIVERSAL_STRING) reads 4 bytes

claims.text: Overwrites stack contents via use-after-free, potentially allowing control-flow hijacking
claims.reasoning: Calling free() on a stack address is undefined behavior that can corrupt the heap allocator's free list, causing subsequent malloc() calls to return stack addresses. This allows attacker-controlled data to overwrite stack contents (return addresses, frame pointers, local variables), enabling control-flow hijacking. This is a well-known exploitation technique.

citations.note: free(buf) on stack address corrupts heap allocator metadata

claims.text: Set up malicious server with TLS certificate that triggers the condition wc >= 0x00200000 during certificate parsing
claims.reasoning: An attacker can craft a certificate with a UniversalString (CURL_ASN1_UNIVERSAL_STRING) containing a 4-byte sequence that decodes to wc >= 0x00200000 (e.g., any value with the high bit of the first byte set). This triggers the bug during TLS handshake certificate parsing.

citations.note: wc built from 4 input bytes for CURL_ASN1_UNIVERSAL_STRING
Condition wc >= 0x00200000 is attacker-controllable via certificate content

key_reasons: The code at lib/vtls/x509asn1.c:378 (master) / :374 (curl-8_8_0) shows buf is a stack-allocated array: 'char buf[4];'
The code at lib/vtls/x509asn1.c:397 (master) / :393 (curl-8_8_0) calls free(buf) on that stack buffer when wc >= 0x00200000
This code path is reachable during TLS certificate parsing for non-UTF8 string types (e.g., CURL_ASN1_UNIVERSAL_STRING) with attacker-controlled certificate data
Calling free() on a stack address corrupts the heap allocator, enabling use-after-free and potential code execution via stack overwrite
The bug exists in both the reported commit and the latest release (curl-8_8_0); master still has it
reply: Thank you for this clear and well-documented report. The code confirms the bug: utf8asn1str() allocates 'char buf[4]' on the stack at line 378 and incorrectly calls free(buf) at line 397 when wc >= 0x00200000. This is reachable via a malicious TLS certificate containing a UniversalString with crafted bytes. The fix (removing the free() call) is correct. This is a valid security vulnerability in the released version curl-8_8_0 and master.
